title: Sequences — 28 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Sequences. 28 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/sequences.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 12 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 16 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 32 pairs; the theorems fall into 15 strands, the largest of 6. Most binding: fib (6), popcount (5), tm (4), choose (2). 11 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: fnv.lean. Built on it: demand.lean, demand3.lean. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/sequences.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 28 sealed receipts fold to ba405d9e-a92b-8525-a8ff-5ac89301f613. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 2, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand2.lean (6 observed, 2.88 expected, lift 2.08), involution.lean (3 observed, 1.92 expected, lift 1.56), rights.lean (3 observed, 1.92 expected, lift 1.56). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.31 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 83.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.28; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.46. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 78375f1a602d (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Cassini’s identity — G. D. Cassini, 1680; Lucas sequences — Édouard Lucas, 1878; the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity — Brahmagupta, 628; Pascal’s triangle mod 2 — Blaise Pascal, 1654. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. cassini_at_even_indices — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => n % 2 == 1 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1) record
  2. cassini_at_odd_indices — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => n % 2 == 0 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n) record
  3. cassini_deviation_is_exactly_one — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun n => (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1) || (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n)) record
  4. lucas_mod_two_is_the_and_rule — (List.range 14).all (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).all (fun k => (choose n k % 2 == 1) == (andN k n == k))) record
  5. pascal_has_both_parities — ((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k % 2))).contains 1 ∧ ((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n => (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k => choose n k % 2))).contains 0 record
  6. sums_of_two_squares_are_closed — (List.range 8).all (fun a => (List.range 8).all (fun b => (List.range 8).all (fun c => (List.range 8).all (fun d => (a*a + b*b) * (c*c + d*d) == (a*c - b*d) * (a*c - b*d) + (a*d + b*c) * (a*d + b*c) || (a*c) < (b*d))))) record
  7. three_five_eight_are_consecutive — fib 4 = 3 ∧ fib 5 = 5 ∧ fib 6 = 8 ∧ fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 6 record
  8. pisano_twentyfour_is_four_sixes — (List.range 30).all (fun k => fib k % 9 == fib (k + 24) % 9) ∧ 24 = 4 * 6 record
  9. thue_morse_doubling_recurrence — (List.range 200).all (fun n => tm (2 * n) == tm n && tm (2 * n + 1) == 1 - tm n) record
  10. doubling_preserves_the_parity_of_the_bits — (List.range 200).all (fun n => popcount (2 * n) == popcount n) record
  11. the_odd_step_sets_exactly_one_further_bit — (List.range 200).all (fun n => popcount (2 * n + 1) == popcount n + 1) record
  12. the_sequence_takes_both_values — ((List.range 200).filter (fun n => tm n == 0)).length = 100 ∧ ((List.range 200).filter (fun n => tm n == 1)).length = 100 record
  13. cassinis_identity_for_every_m — ∀ m : Nat, fib (2 * m + 1) * fib (2 * m + 3) = fib (2 * m + 2) * fib (2 * m + 2) + 1 ∧ fib (2 * m) * fib (2 * m + 2) + 1 = fib (2 * m + 1) * fib (2 * m + 1) record
  14. a_bit_sum_over_one_more_position_adds_that_bit — ∀ F m : Nat, (List.range (F + 1)).foldl (fun a i => a + m / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 = (List.range F).foldl (fun a i => a + m / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 + m / 2 ^ F % 2 record
  15. halving_shifts_every_bit_down_by_one — ∀ m i : Nat, m / 2 ^ (i + 1) = m / 2 / 2 ^ i record
  16. the_bits_of_a_number_are_its_low_bit_then_the_bits_of_its_half — ∀ F m : Nat, (List.range (F + 1)).foldl (fun a i => a + m / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 = m % 2 + (List.range F).foldl (fun a i => a + m / 2 / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 record
  17. bits_above_the_number_add_nothing — ∀ k F n : Nat, n < 2 ^ F → (List.range (F + k)).foldl (fun a i => a + n / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 = (List.range F).foldl (fun a i => a + n / 2 ^ i % 2) 0 record
  18. a_number_is_below_two_to_its_own_power — ∀ n : Nat, n < 2 ^ n record
  19. a_number_is_below_two_to_its_own_successor — ∀ n : Nat, n < 2 ^ (n + 1) record
  20. doubling_preserves_the_bit_count_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, popcount (2 * n) = popcount n record
  21. the_odd_step_sets_exactly_one_further_bit_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, popcount (2 * n + 1) = popcount n + 1 record
  22. thue_morse_doubling_recurrence_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, tm (2 * n) = tm n ∧ tm (2 * n + 1) = 1 - tm n record
  23. halving_removes_exactly_the_low_bit_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, popcount n = n % 2 + popcount (n / 2) record
  24. the_thue_morse_halving_recurrence_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, tm n = (n % 2 + tm (n / 2)) % 2 record
  25. doubling_shifts_every_bit_up_by_one — ∀ m i : Nat, 2 * m / 2 ^ (i + 1) = m / 2 ^ i record
  26. the_residue_below_the_next_power_adds_one_bit — ∀ m F : Nat, m % 2 ^ (F + 1) = m % 2 ^ F + m / 2 ^ F % 2 * 2 ^ F record
  27. the_low_bits_rebuild_the_number_below_every_power — ∀ F m : Nat, (List.range F).foldl (fun a i => a + m / 2 ^ i % 2 * 2 ^ i) 0 = m % 2 ^ F record
  28. the_number_is_rebuilt_from_its_bits_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, (List.range (n + 1)).foldl (fun a i => a + n / 2 ^ i % 2 * 2 ^ i) 0 = n record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 78375f1a602d and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
